resale_co.name: Resale Certificate of Occupancy (resale inspection)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Beach Haven Zoning Department (Construction and Zoning)
resale_co.lead_time: Allow 2 weeks to schedule the inspection; resale inspections are done Tuesday and Thursday afternoons
requirements: Visual inspection only, not a structural inspection
General condition of the lot, exterior and interior
Porch, deck and stair condition
Smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarm(s)
Acceptable electrical and plumbing systems
Proper venting of heating equipment
Relief valves on water heaters and boilers piped down to within 6 inches of the floor (no plastic or galvanized pipe); water heater cabinets open for the inspection
Proper fire separation between an attached garage and living areas
Bedroom windows open easily for escape
House numbers on the building (3 inch numbers for homes)
Door locks on exit doors work and are not double-keyed
Portable fire extinguisher (2A:10B:C, no more than 10 lbs) mounted within 10 feet of the kitchen and no more than 5 feet above the floor (still listed on the Borough's 2024 sheet)
Current plot plan survey and flood elevation certificate with raised seals in the buyer's name
No open permits: all open permits must be finaled before the resale inspection
Property must be unoccupied, alarm systems disabled and dogs removed or crated at the inspection

fees.label: Resale Certificate of Occupancy, each residential unit
fees.quote: Resale Certificate of Occupancy Each Residential Unit $75.00

resale_co.how_to_apply: Bring the completed Resale Certificate of Occupancy form, the other listed paperwork (current plot plan and elevation certificate, filed deed restriction, condominium certification if a condo), a check made out to the Borough of Beach Haven and property access information to the Construction and Zoning office, 300 Engleside Avenue (the form also lists cash). The deed restriction must be filed with the Ocean County Clerk's Office in Toms River.

resale_co.notes: Fees are on the Construction and Zoning page fee table (each residential unit $75.00, each commercial unit $150.00, reinspection $20.00) and on the 2023 Resale Certificate of Occupancy form (single $75.00, duplex $150.00, commercial $150.00, re-inspect $20.00). The Borough's 2024 resale requirements sheet still requires a mounted portable fire extinguisher; the state dropped the extinguisher from the state sale certificate in February 2025 (P.L.2025, c.19), but this is the Borough's own resale checklist, so confirm with the office. Resident Emergency Access Placards (all non-condo owners) must be present and visible at the inspection and left for the new owner. Rental properties are separate: yearly landlord registration with the Borough and a county fire inspection certificate for each rental season or tenant change.

requirements: Smoke alarms on every living level including the basement, and within 10 feet of bedrooms on levels with bedrooms
All smoke alarms, including hardwired, must be under 10 years old
Battery-only smoke alarms must be 10-year sealed battery units (since January 1, 2019); homes built before 1978 need at least one on each level
Homes built 1978 to 1983 need hardwired alarms on each level; 1984 to 1990 interconnected hardwired alarms with battery backup on each level; 1991 and later also in every bedroom
Hardwired alarms that need replacing must be replaced with hardwired alarms, not battery alarms
Carbon monoxide alarm near the sleeping areas if the home has a fuel-burning appliance or an attached garage; battery and plug-in CO alarms should be under 5 years old

Homes with a generator, solar panels or battery storage need a printed caution label (for example CAUTION: MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER) within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and the electric meter
A monitored low-voltage fire alarm system needs an NFPA 72 test report sent to the Fire Marshal before closing
Portable fire extinguishers are no longer required (as of February 3, 2025)
Do not mount alarms in unfinished attics, garages, stairwells, the top of basement stairs or kitchens

authorities.lead_time: Apply more than 10 business days before closing for the lowest fee; the office calls to schedule the inspection after the application is submitted. The certificate is valid 12 months from the inspection.

fire_cert.notes: The Ocean County Fire Marshal is Beach Haven's fire code enforcing agency (registry code C), and its Resale and Rental Home Inspections page lists Beach Haven for resales and rentals of 1-2 family buildings, so it is recorded as the resale smoke/CO certificate issuer. Two signs point to a possible change: the Borough's Construction and Zoning page (updated 2026-09-14) says a link to schedule the Smoke/CO Inspection from the 'Beach Haven Fire Inspector' is 'COMING SOON', and the state fire directory names 'Beach Haven Boro' (300 Engleside Av, phone printed as (732) 492-0111) in the smoke detector compliance column. Confirm with the Borough (609-492-0111) or the Fire Marshal ((732) 929-2088) who is doing resale smoke/CO inspections at the time of sale. The Borough's own resale inspection also checks smoke and CO alarms. Beach Haven Volunteer Fire Co. (beachhavenfire.com) posts no certificate information.

other_items.label: Deed restriction

other_items.label: Plot plan survey and flood elevation certificate
other_items.detail: Current plot plan survey and flood elevation certificate with raised seals in the buyer's name.

other_items.label: Open permits
other_items.detail: All open permits must be finaled before the resale inspection.

other_items.label: Condominium certification
other_items.detail: Condo units use the Borough's Condominium Certification form listed with the resale paperwork.

other_items.label: Emergency access placard
other_items.detail: Resident Emergency Access Placards (non-condo owners) must be visible at the inspection and left in the property for the new owner.
